question: Can a disposable SQLite projection preserve Promptus's current logical behavior while removing enough repeated derived-cache work to justify a production development branch?
non_goals: SQLite does not become authoritative; Markdown remains the only source of truth.
The experiment does not change or release shipped Promptus code.
The experiment does not replace the existing lexical ranking with FTS5 or another ranking function.
The experiment does not treat an O(1) cache-generation receipt as proof against out-of-band Markdown edits.

corpus.capture_rule: Accept a snapshot only when source-before, source-after, and copied-store canonical hashes match.

profiles.name: native-ext4-shadow
profiles.purpose: Isolate software work from the already-measured WSL 9p metadata penalty.

implementations.current: CATALOG.md + graph.json + exact bounded lexical search.json rebuilt by kb-index
implementations.candidate: One disposable SQLite file containing normalized units, graph facts, exact lexical postings, and a content-hashed source manifest
implementations.sqlite_durability: Clean builds use a temporary database and atomic rename. Incremental trials use an explicit transaction. No WAL assumption is permitted.

scenarios: fresh JSON parse versus fresh SQLite connection
primary_invariants: The source store hash is unchanged by all non-scenario trials.
SQLite and the current search index return the same ordered keys and bit-stable scores for every query case.
The database's canonical logical digest equals a fresh Markdown projection after one and ten writes.
Deleting and rebuilding the database reproduces the same canonical logical digest and query digests.
An out-of-band Markdown edit is detected by exact content verification and is never represented as authoritative freshness by the experiment.

query_suite.selection: A fixed mix of generic Promptus terms, required/all/status/history filters, and deterministic title-derived phrase cases. Private query text is omitted from the public receipt; query hashes and result digests are retained.
query_suite.equivalence: All ordered result keys must match and floating-point scores must have identical IEEE-754 string representations.

required: Writer-known one-write and ten-write SQLite transactions are at least 5x faster than a full current re-index on the same snapshot.
Fresh-connection SQLite retrieval is no slower than fresh JSON parse plus the same exact ranking.
The result identifies a fail-closed strategy for out-of-band Markdown changes without calling SQLite authoritative.
decision_rule.interpretation: Passing supports a narrow derived-cache development branch, not adoption or release. Failing any correctness invariant rejects the candidate regardless of speed.

privacy: The snapshot and database remain in temporary local storage. The committed receipt contains aggregate timings, counts, and hashes only; it contains no MoT unit bodies, titles, paths, query text, or retrieval results.
